skill.name: xhs-competitor-research-v2
skill.description: Guides keyword-based Xiaohongshu competitor research through SocialDataX, with search filters, bounded pagination, and evidence-based content comparisons.
skill.summary: Compare Xiaohongshu content samples, creator positioning, and topic angles using SocialDataX search.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts match Markdown formatting, documented service links, or legitimate API key configuration rather than malicious behavior. The command example executes an unpinned npm package, and separate instructions require unrestricted forwarding of token-bearing result URLs. No evidence found of audit manipulation, embedded secrets, or deliberate credential exfiltration in the reviewed files; external package implementation was not included.

remediation.issue: The direct CLI example automatically executes socialdatax-skills@latest with access to the runtime environment.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and verify package provenance before execution. Require approval for installation and provide only the required service credential.

remediation.issue: Result URLs must retain xsec_token during every display, storage, and forwarding operation, without considering destination or sensitivity.
remediation.suggestion: Keep complete links only in authorized research contexts. Explain token sensitivity and require approval before external sharing; permit redaction in public reports and logs.

content.value_statement: Competitor content research needs relevant samples and clear limits on coverage. This skill guides SocialDataX searches and separates visible evidence from content strategy judgments.
actual_capabilities: Guides keyword-based Xiaohongshu searches through the SocialDataX CLI or xhs_search_notes MCP tool.
Documents sorting by time, likes, comments, or collections, with image, video, and publication-time filters.
Supports bounded research workflows using page counts, item limits, and opaque continuation tokens.
Documents recent-day filtering within the retrieved search pages rather than claiming complete platform coverage.
Structures content samples, topic angles, audience feedback, and creator positioning with evidence separated from interpretation.
Provides recovery rules for partial results, network errors, and insufficient service balance.
limitations: Requires a SocialDataX API key, network access, and available service balance; direct CLI use also requires Node.js and npm.
The supplied files contain instructions, not the external CLI implementation; runtime behavior and package integrity were not verified.
Search results are bounded samples and cannot establish complete platform coverage or prove why content performed well.
The documented workflow does not log in, publish, like, comment, or modify accounts.

use_cases.title: Compare Brand Content Angles
use_cases.description: Review keyword-based competitor samples and compare recurring topics, positioning, and visible audience responses.

use_cases.title: Review Creator Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare creator samples within a niche and identify content differences supported by retrieved evidence.

use_cases.title: Plan New Topic Directions
use_cases.description: Explore recent niche samples and identify focused questions for the next content planning session.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Topic
prompt_templates.prompt: Research Xiaohongshu posts about beginner running shoes using one search page. Summarize relevant titles, authors, and content angles.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Brand Angles
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Xiaohongshu content about Brand A and Brand B running shoes. Limit each search to one page and separate evidence from interpretation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recent Video Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Research running shoe videos from the last seven days. Search at most three pages and collect at most 30 results, sorted by comments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine recency, format, sorting, and collection limits.

prompt_templates.title: Recover and Synthesize Partial Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue this partial competitor search using its returned token and unchanged filters. Subtract collected pages and items from the original limits. Report gaps and evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: resume bounded research without restarting completed pages.

output_examples.input: Compare beginner running shoe content for two brands using one page per brand.
output: Illustrative report format, not live search results.
Brand A sample: retrieved title, author, and note reference.
Brand B sample: retrieved title, author, and note reference.
Comparison: distinguish observed content angles from proposed positioning explanations.
Coverage: one search page per brand; findings do not represent the full platform.

output_examples.input: Summarize a recent-topic search that stopped after partial results.
output: Illustrative recovery summary, not a live API response.
Status: incomplete; retain collected samples and the reported error.
Recovery: continue only with the returned nonempty token and unchanged query filters.
Limits: deduct completed pages and collected items before requesting more results.
Conclusion: mark missing evidence and avoid platform-wide trend claims.

best_practices: Start with one page and focused keywords, then expand within explicit page and item limits.
Keep query filters unchanged when resuming pagination, and label partial results clearly.
Use a reviewed CLI version and protect API keys and token-bearing links when storing or sharing research.
anti_patterns: Treating a few returned pages as complete platform coverage or proof of content performance causes.
Restarting partial searches from page one without accounting for completed work and service costs.
Publishing API keys or forwarding token-bearing result links to unauthorized destinations.

faq.question: What inputs does this skill support?
faq.answer: Start with a keyword or topic direction. Add brand, audience, scenario, content type, or time filters to narrow the sample.

faq.question: Do I need a SocialDataX account?
faq.answer: You need a SocialDataX API key configured as SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY and sufficient service balance. Direct CLI use also requires Node.js and npm.

faq.question: Can I use MCP instead of the CLI?
faq.answer: Yes, the instructions document xhs_search_notes as an alternative. An available, configured MCP integration is required.

faq.question: Does recent-day filtering cover all Xiaohongshu posts?
faq.answer: No. The recent-day filter applies within retrieved search pages. Page limits and available publication timestamps constrain coverage.

faq.question: Can this skill publish or manage my account?
faq.answer: The documented workflow is read-only. It excludes login, posting, likes, comments, browser data access, and account changes.

faq.question: What happens when a search returns partial results?
faq.answer: Keep collected items and the error. Resume only with a nonempty returned token, unchanged filters, and remaining page and item limits.
